          UPON hearing the counsel the Court made the following
                             O R D E R
1. In continuation of previous orders, the High-Powered Enquiry
Committee (HPEC) submitted its status report dated 06.10.2026. It
is informed that the first meeting of the Committee was convened on
01.09.2026 and thereafter a space to operate as the Secretariat has
been identified, where necessary repair work is ongoing. Mr.
Srinivasa Kammath R, a retired Joint Registrar (Law) from the
National Human Rights Commission (NHRC), has been appointed as the
Member Secretary of the Committee.
10

--- Page 26 ---
2. It is pointed out that the HPEC has vide its letter dated
13.09.2026 made the following requests to the Ministry of Home
Affairs (MHA): (i) Server of adequate capacity to be installed in
the server room being made ready in the proposed office; (ii) a
suitable portal developed through NIC to facilitate the aggrieved
persons to upload their complaints; (iii) a new generator of
adequate load bearing capacity installed at premises allotted; and
(iv) minimum Secretariat staff comprising of 01 IT professional, 01
Section Officer, 02 Assistant Section Officers, 02 Data Entry
Operators, 02 Stenographers, 01 Hindi Translator and 03 Multi-
Tasking Staff (MTS).
3. With respect to the above urgent requirements of the HPEC, the
learned Solicitor General of India assured that if any facility is
not available so far, the needful shall be done without any delay.
4. The  status  report  further  reveals  that  the  National
Informatics Centre (NIC) has been engaged for the design and
development of the portal and the two standard templates, one each
for the aggrieved protesters and another for aggrieved police
personnel, have been provided to the NIC along with relevant
materials. The NIC has been instructed to ensure strict provisions
for anonymity and confidentiality of complaints, evidence, and
statements so as to protect vulnerable witnesses and keep their
identities undisclosed.
5. We direct the NIC, through the MHA, to design and develop the
portal according to the HPEC's requirements, ensuring all specified
witness protection measures are integrated. The Committee informed
the Court that the portal, fully equipped with all necessary
11

--- Page 27 ---
features, is complete and scheduled for launch next week. Public
notices will subsequently be published in major national newspapers
to widely announce its launch.
6. As  highlighted  in  the  status  report,  certain  essential
facilities  are  still  required  for  the  smooth  and  seamless
functioning of the HPEC. The MHA is directed to take necessary
steps to provide these facilities.
7. Dr. Monika Gusain, learned Senior Counsel and Amicus Curiae
representing the HPEC, stated that she will inform the committee
that  first  Action  Taken  Report  in  terms  of  the  priorities
highlighted in our order dated 10.09.2026 be submitted for further
consideration.  
8. Counter affidavit, if any, be filed within three weeks.
9. List on 02.11.2026.
T.P.(Crl.) No. 836/2026
1. The Transfer Petition is allowed in terms of the signed order.
2. The Registrar General of the Delhi High Court is directed to
ensure that the original records are transferred to this Court
forthwith. In this regard, the Secretary General of this Court may
coordinate with the Registrar General of the Delhi High Court to
facilitate a prompt transfer of the original records to this Court.
3. Consequentially, pending I.As, if any, also stand disposed of.
(NITIN TALREJA)                            (PREETHI DILEEP KUMAR)

          UPON hearing the counsel the Court made the following
                             O R D E R
1. In continuation of previous orders, the High-Powered Enquiry
Committee (HPEC) submitted its status report dated 06.10.2026. It
is informed that the first meeting of the Committee was convened on
01.09.2026 and thereafter a space to operate as the Secretariat has
been identified, where necessary repair work is ongoing. Mr.
Srinivasa Kammath R, a retired Joint Registrar (Law) from the
22

--- Page 38 ---
National Human Rights Commission (NHRC), has been appointed as the
Member Secretary of the Committee.
2. It is pointed out that the HPEC has vide its letter dated
13.09.2026 made the following requests to the Ministry of Home
Affairs (MHA): (i) Server of adequate capacity to be installed in
the server room being made ready in the proposed office; (ii) a
suitable portal developed through NIC to facilitate the aggrieved
persons to upload their complaints; (iii) a new generator of
adequate load bearing capacity installed at premises allotted; and
(iv) minimum Secretariat staff comprising of 01 IT professional, 01
Section Officer, 02 Assistant Section Officers, 02 Data Entry
Operators, 02 Stenographers, 01 Hindi Translator and 03 Multi-
Tasking Staff (MTS).
3. With respect to the above urgent requirements of the HPEC, the
learned Solicitor General of India assured that if any facility is
not available so far, the needful shall be done without any delay.
4. The  status  report  further  reveals  that  the  National
Informatics Centre (NIC) has been engaged for the design and
development of the portal and the two standard templates, one each
for the aggrieved protesters and another for aggrieved police
personnel, have been provided to the NIC along with relevant
materials. The NIC has been instructed to ensure strict provisions
for anonymity and confidentiality of complaints, evidence, and
statements so as to protect vulnerable witnesses and keep their
identities undisclosed.
5. We direct the NIC, through the MHA, to design and develop the
portal according to the HPEC's requirements, ensuring all specified
23

--- Page 39 ---
witness protection measures are integrated. The Committee informed
the Court that the portal, fully equipped with all necessary
features, is complete and scheduled for launch next week. Public
notices will subsequently be published in major national newspapers
to widely announce its launch.
6. As  highlighted  in  the  status  report,  certain  essential
facilities  are  still  required  for  the  smooth  and  seamless
functioning of the HPEC. The MHA is directed to take necessary
steps to provide these facilities.
7. Dr. Monika Gusain, learned Senior Counsel and Amicus Curiae
representing the HPEC, stated that she will inform the committee
that  first  Action  Taken  Report  in  terms  of  the  priorities
highlighted in our order dated 10.09.2026 be submitted for further
consideration.  
8. Counter affidavit, if any, be filed within three weeks.
9. List on 02.11.2026.
T.P.(Crl.) No. 836/2026
10. Since the matter pending before the Delhi High Court already
stands transferred to this Court, we request the Hon'ble Chief
Justice of the Delhi High Court to ensure the immediate transfer of
records to this Court's registry, if already not transferred. The
Secretary General of this Court will coordinate with the Registrar
General of the Delhi High Court to facilitate a prompt transfer
without delay.
(NITIN TALREJA)                            (PREETHI DILEEP KUMAR)

Mr. Sankalp Mahindru, Adv.                      
          UPON hearing the counsel the Court made the following
                             O R D E R
1. In continuation of previous orders, the High-Powered Enquiry
Committee (HPEC) submitted its status report dated 06.10.2026. It
is informed that the first meeting of the Committee was convened on
01.09.2026 and thereafter a space to operate as the Secretariat has
been identified, where necessary repair work is ongoing. Mr.
Srinivasa Kammath R, a retired Joint Registrar (Law) from the
National Human Rights Commission (NHRC), has been appointed as the
Member Secretary of the Committee.
2. It is pointed out that the HPEC has vide its letter dated
13.09.2026 made the following requests to the Ministry of Home
Affairs (MHA): (i) Server of adequate capacity to be installed in
34

--- Page 50 ---
the server room being made ready in the proposed office; (ii) a
suitable portal developed through NIC to facilitate the aggrieved
persons to upload their complaints; (iii) a new generator of
adequate load bearing capacity installed at premises allotted; and
(iv) minimum Secretariat staff comprising of 01 IT professional, 01
Section Officer, 02 Assistant Section Officers, 02 Data Entry
Operators, 02 Stenographers, 01 Hindi Translator and 03 Multi-
Tasking Staff (MTS).
3. With respect to the above urgent requirements of the HPEC, the
learned Solicitor General of India assured that if any facility is
not available so far, the needful shall be done without any delay.
4. The  status  report  further  reveals  that  the  National
Informatics Centre (NIC) has been engaged for the design and
development of the portal and the two standard templates, one each
for the aggrieved protesters and another for aggrieved police
personnel, have been provided to the NIC along with relevant
materials. The NIC has been instructed to ensure strict provisions
for anonymity and confidentiality of complaints, evidence, and
statements so as to protect vulnerable witnesses and keep their
identities undisclosed.
5. We direct the NIC, through the MHA, to design and develop the
portal according to the HPEC's requirements, ensuring all specified
witness protection measures are integrated. The Committee informed
the Court that the portal, fully equipped with all necessary
features, is complete and scheduled for launch next week. Public
notices will subsequently be published in major national newspapers
to widely announce its launch.
35

--- Page 51 ---
6. As  highlighted  in  the  status  report,  certain  essential
facilities  are  still  required  for  the  smooth  and  seamless
functioning of the HPEC. The MHA is directed to take necessary
steps to provide these facilities.
7. Dr. Menaka Guruswamy, learned Senior Counsel representing the
HPEC, stated that she will inform the committee that first Action
Taken Report in terms of the priorities highlighted in our order
dated 10.09.2026 be submitted for further consideration.  
8. Counter affidavit, if any, be filed within three weeks.
9. List on 02.11.2026.
T.P.(Crl.) No. 836/2026
10. Since the matter pending before the Delhi High Court already
stands transferred to this Court, we request the Hon'ble Chief
Justice of the Delhi High Court to ensure the immediate transfer of
records to this Court's registry, if already not transferred. The
Secretary General of this Court will coordinate with the Registrar
General of the Delhi High Court to facilitate a prompt transfer
without delay.
(NITIN TALREJA)                            (PREETHI DILEEP KUMAR)
ASTT. REGISTRAR-cum-PS                        DY. REGISTRAR

     UPON hearing the counsel the Court made the following
                             O R D E R
Item No.-301.1 Diary No. 39789/2026
1. The applicant (petitioner in contempt) appearing-in-person
has  preferred  this  Contempt  Petition  in  the  main  matter
bringing it to our notice that the order passed by this Court
dated  17.4.2025  in  I.A.  No.260997  of  2024  has  not  been
complied with till this point of time.  The order, referred to
above, reads thus:-
"11. The learned ASG states that the process of
publication of Annual Report on road accidents in
2023 is going on. We grant time to the MoRTH to
publish the by the end of August 2025. We also
direct  the  MoRTH  to  ensure  that  such  annual
reports are published within a period of six
months from expiry of every calendar year. Only if
such reports are published with promptness, the
same can be useful.
12. The Application is, accordingly, disposed of.”
2. It appears that this Court said something about the
process of publication of annual report on road accidents in
8

--- Page 92 ---
2023 which was an ongoing process.  This Court granted time to
MoRTH to publish the same by the end of August, 2025.   MoRTH
was also directed to ensure that such annual reports are
published within a period of six months from expiry of every
calendar year.  This Court laid emphasis on the fact that only
if such reports are published with promptness, the same would
be useful. 
3. Issue notice, returnable on 25.11.2026.
4. Union to reply as to why this direction issued by this
Court has not been complied with so far and what they propose
to do. 
Item No. 301.2-Diary No. 40407/2026
1. The applicant (petitioner in contempt) has preferred this
Contempt Petition in the main matter bringing it to our notice
that  despite  there  being  a  specific  order  passed  by  a
Coordinate  Bench  of  this  Court  dated  28.4.2025  in
I.A. No.76249 of 2024, no steps have been taken by the Central
Government to frame a scheme for grant of interim relief to
the claimants.
2. Section 164A of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 provides for
a Scheme for Interim Relief for claimants.
9

--- Page 93 ---
3. The order dated 28.4.2025, referred to above, reads thus:-
"4. Section 164A of the MV Act reads thus:
164-A. Scheme for interim relief for claimants.—(1)
The Central Government, may make schemes for the
provision of interim relief to claimants praying for
compensation under this Chapter.
(2) A scheme made under sub-section (1) shall also
provide   procedure to recover funds disbursed under
such scheme from the owner of the motor vehicle, where
the claim arises out of the use of such motor vehicle
or other sources as may be prescribed by the Central
Government.
5. Though Section 164A was brought into force on 1st
April, 2022, for a period of three years, the Central
Government has not implemented the same by framing a
scheme for interim relief for the claimants. Under the
earlier  Motor  Vehicles  Act,  the  Tribunals  were
empowered  to  grant  such  interim  relief.  Such  an
important  provision  like  Section  164A  has  remain
unimplemented for last three years. This failure has
to be deprecated. We, therefore, direct the Central
Government to frame a scheme under Section 164A of the
MV Act as expeditiously as possible and, in any event,
within a period of four months from today.
6. The Application is disposed of."
4. Mr. Vikramjit Banerjee, the learned ASG appearing for the
Union brought to our notice that the Government of India in
its Ministry of Road Transport and Highways has framed the
Scheme  under  Section  164A  of  the  Act,  1988  titled
"Compensation to Victims (Interim Relief) Scheme, 2026". He
invited our attention, more particularly to clause 6 of the
10

--- Page 94 ---
Scheme.  Clause 6 reads thus: -
"6.  Procedure  for  receiving  interim  compensation
6.1. The claimant (victim or the legal heir/s of the deceased)
shall make an application seeking interim compensation in Form
I,  through  electronic  portal  designated  by  the  Central
Government  along  with  the  details  of  application  for
compensation  filed/pending  before  the  Claims  Tribunal.
6.2. The application form shall also include undertakings, to
be signed by the claimant(s), affirming that they are the
rightful claimant(s) and accepting the liability to return the
amount received as interim compensation, in case the Claims
Tribunal  passes  an  order  against  the  claimant(s).
6.3. Upon receipt of the application for interim relief on the
portal, the same shall be electronically transmitted to both
the Department of Financial Services ("DFS"), Ministry of
Finance,  Government  of  India  and  to  the  concerned
Investigating Officer. DFS shall electronically transmit the
application to the Insurance Company of vehicle involved in
the  accident.
6.4. The investigating officer shall upload the DAR on the
aforementioned designated portal, within 90 days from the date
of accident, as prescribed under clause 12 of the Annexure
XIII  of  Central  Motor  Vehicles  Rules,  1989  ("CMVR").
6.5. The Insurance Company shall, within thirty days from the
date of uploading of the DAR on the aforementioned designated
portal  by  the  Investigating  Officer,  either  accept  the
application or reject the same, with reasons recorded in Form
II. If the insurance company neither accepts nor rejects the
application within the said time and subsequently accepts
liability, the payment shall be made along with interest at a
rate determined by the Central Government. Form II shall be
uploaded on the portal and the details shall also be submitted
to the Claims Tribunal before which the application for
compensation, is pending.
6.6. Where the insurance company accepts the liability, the
payment shall be made before the Claims Tribunal within 30
days from the date of acceptance on the portal in Form II and
the  said  Tribunal  shall  record  such  payment.
6.7. If the claimant and the insurance company agree upon a
settlement and payment under Section 149(3)(a) or no fault
11

--- Page 95 ---
liability disbursement under Section 164, then the pending
application  for  interim  compensation  shall  lapse.
6.8. The amount of interim compensation paid shall be deducted
from the amount of settlement recorded subsequently between
the insurance company and the claimant under point 6.7, at the
time  of  award  of  settlement.
6.9. The amount of interim compensation paid shall be taken
into account by the Claims Tribunal in case it passes an award
under  Section  168  granting  compensation.  Any  interim
compensation amount so paid shall be deducted from the final
compensation  awarded  by  the  Claims  Tribunal.
6.10. If any amount for interim relief has been paid to the
claimant and subsequently, the Claims Tribunal passes an order
against such claimant, the interim relief amount shall be
recoverable. In such cases, the Claims Tribunal shall be
competent to pass an order for recovery from the claimant to
whom such interim relief was paid, in favour of the insurance
company that has paid such interim relief."
5. He also invited our attention to a letter dated 23.2.2026
addressed  by  the  Director  (MVL)  to  the  Chief
Secretaries/Administrators  of  States/Union  Territories  and
other  departments  with  the  subject  circulation  of
"Compensation to Victims (Interim Relief) Scheme 2026". 
6. Mr. Gaurav Agrawal, the learned  Amicus as well as the
applicant would submit that they had no idea about this scheme
being framed by the Union. However, the learned Amicus, and
the applicant appearing in person brought to our notice that
this scheme is applicable only in cases of claims arising out
of the use of Motor Vehicles which are insured.  
12

--- Page 96 ---
7. To  put  it  in  other  words,  the  amount  for  interim
compensation would be paid by the authorised insurer of the
vehicle involved in the accident. According to both, this
scheme does not take care of uninsured vehicles where the
driver of the vehicle can be asked to pay the compensation. 
8. We request Mr. Banerjee to take appropriate instructions
in this regard as to whether this Scheme would also include
non-insured vehicles or not. Besides, we want the Union to
ensure  that  people  at  large  come  to  know  about  this
Compensation Scheme, 2026.  People should know because it is a
beneficial piece of legislation. A common man will not come to
know unless made aware that he has a right under the Scheme to
pray for compensation by way of interim relief. What steps
should be taken in this regard is for the Union to look into.
However, we direct the Union to give wide publicity about this
Compensation to Victims (Interim Relief) Scheme, 2026.
9. We may draw the attention of the Union to Section 212 of
the  Act,  1988.   Section  212  provides  for  publication,
commencement  and  laying  of  Rules  and  notifications.  Sub-
section 2 of Section 212 provides that all rules made under
this Act shall be published in the Official Gazette, and shall
unless some later date is appointed, come into force on the
13

--- Page 97 ---
date  of  such  publication.  Sub-section  3  of  Section  212
provides that every rule made by any State Government shall be
laid, as soon as may be after it is made before the State
Legislature.  This Scheme is a statutory scheme because it is
framed under statutory provision of Section 164A of the Act,
1988. Section 2 (38-A) defines the term Scheme- it means a
Scheme framed under this Act.  This being a statutory scheme
framed under Section 164A of the Act, the same would be
covered under Section 212 of the Act, 1988. 
10. Union shall see to it that the Scheme is published in the
Official Gazette at the earliest.  
11. By the next date of hearing, Union shall give us a fair
idea how they propose to make it operational.
12. The applicant-in-person has some suggestions which the
Union  may  consider  for  effective  implementation  of  this
particular Scheme.  The suggestions are as under:-
"(i) Collection and publication of data by MoRTH:
MoRTH may be directed to collect district-wise data
from the State Governments/UTs, the High Courts,
IRDAI and insurers on:
a) claims pending before the Motor Accident Claims
Tribunals under Section 166 of the MV Act;
b) appeals pending before the High Courts under
14

--- Page 98 ---
Section 173 of the Act;
c) proceedings pending for recovery of compensation
awarded; and
d) awards of the Tribunals and orders of the High
Courts that remain unsatisfied.
(ii)  Identification  of  Bottlenecks:  The  State
Governments/UT /authorities concerned shall furnish the
above information to MoRTH in the prescribed form within
thirty days of the end of each quarter. MoRTH shall, in
turn, publish consolidated district-wise, State/UT-wise
and national statistics every quarter, within forty-five
days of the end of the quarter. MoRTH and the State
Governments/UTs shall examine these statistics. The aim
is  to  identify  bottlenecks  and  make  the  system
efficient,  time-bound  and  result-oriented,  so  that
compensation  actually  reaches  victims  and  their
dependents without delay.
(iii) Infrastructure for Claims Tribunals: The State
Governments shall, in consultation with the respective
High Courts, provide adequate infrastructure for the
efficient functioning of the Claims Tribunals, including
presiding officers, supporting staff, courtrooms and
digital facilities. The need is acute in States such as
Uttar Pradesh, where claims take on average more than
five years to be decided and the Tribunals are reported
to face serious infrastructural constraints."
15

--- Page 99 ---
13. Union shall look into the same and revert by the next date
of hearing.

Heard learned Senior Counsel for the petitioners and
learned Counsel for the respondents.
2. Having considered the matter in its entirety and also
in the peculiar facts and circumstances of the present
cases, we find that the orders impugned do not need
interference.
3. We further note that the impugned order(s) has been
passed on a stand taken by the learned Counsel for the
petitioners before the learned Single Judge of the High
Court with regard to the present private respondents being
similarly situated to the person in whose favour the
Courts have passed an order and which has been upheld till
this Court and no ground has been taken refuting such
concession, even before the Division Bench or even this
Court.
4. Accordingly, reiterating the fact that in the peculiar
facts and circumstances of the present cases, the Special
Leave Petitions stand dismissed.
5. After the order was dictated, learned Senior Counsel
for the petitioners submits that the directions passed in
matters  which  were  dismissed  earlier  by  order  dated
20.08.2026 in SLP(Civil) No.1745/2024, the liability of
11

--- Page 124 ---
SLP (C) NO. 1258/2024
the petitioner-University may be limited to what has been
observed in the said order.
6. Having regard to the aforesaid, we indicate that as
the present matters being dismissed in similar terms, the
said  clarification  as  recorded  in  the  order  dated

to the present cases also.

O R D E R
The matter has been listed on motion made by Mr. Ranjit Kumar,
learned  Senior  Counsel,  who  was  requested  by  the  Court  on
23.09.2026 to assist with regard to the main issue, on the plea
that the Court had finally granted indulgence across the board by
not issuing notice of contempt and requiring only an affidavit on
merits to be filed by all the persons concerned, but inadvertently,
the same position was not reflected in the order which was finally
uploaded.

--- Page 133 ---
9
SLP (C) No. 5582/2023
2. It has been pointed out that in the said order, notice of
contempt has also been issued to various respondents.
3. Having regard to the aforesaid, without going into the details
of such references, in general, we direct that for the present, no
contempt notice shall be issued to any party, which obviously gives
them exemption from appearance. However, this will not apply to
respondent No. 93, who, in terms of paragraphs No. 15 to 17 of the
order dated 23.09.2026 shall be personally present. All contempt
notices which may have been reflected in the said order stand
withdrawn. 
4. However, all the parties shall file their fresh up-to-date
affidavits on merits of the issue, personally affirmed by the
Managing  Director/Chief  Executive  Officer/Whole-time
Director/Chairman of such institution.
5. There appears to be some discrepancy with regard to the
appearance of respondents No. 77 and 93, in recording that even
they had also not appeared, which factually is not correct.
6. Accordingly, their names stand deleted from paragraph No. 7 of
the order dated 23.09.2026 which wrongly recorded their non-
appearance.
7. List on usual date i.e. 27.11.2026 at 2.00 p.m.

CIVIL APPELLATE JURISDICTION
CIVIL APPEAL NOS.13877-13878 OF 2026
(Arising out of S.L.P.(Civil) Nos.32164-32165 of 2026)
SARITA SHAILENDRA TIWARI & ANR.  ... APPELLANT(S) 
                  VS.
AXIS BANK LIMITED  ... RESPONDENT(S)
                                                         
          O R D E R
1. Leave granted.
2. Heard Mr. Arijit Prasad, learned senior counsel
appearing for the appellants and Mr. Anupam Lal Das,
learned senior counsel appearing for the respondent-Bank
and Mr.  Naveen Chomal, learned counsel appearing for the
intervenor/auction purchaser.
3. The  present  appeals  call  in  question  the
correctness of the orders dated 5 th August, 2026 and 18 th
August, 2026 passed by the High Court of Judicature at
Bombay in Writ Petition No.9738 of 2026.
4. The appellants availed credit facility from the
respondent-Bank  in  the  year  2021.  Since  there  was
default, on 18th September, 2025, the bank issued a notice
under  Section  13(2)  of  the  Securitisation  and
1

--- Page 143 ---
Reconstruction of Financial Assets and Enforcement of
Security Interest Act, 2002 (for short, “the Act”).
5. It is not disputed before us that after a Section
13(2) notice, demanding a sum of Rs. 4,01,36,821, on 10 th
January, 2025, the bank took symbolic possession under
Section 13(4) of the Act.
6. Thereafter, the appellants filed a Securitisation
Application being SA No. 578 of 2025 before the Debts
Recovery Tribunal-III, Mumbai (for short, “the DRT”)
challenging the demand notice dated 15 th July, 2025, the
possession notice dated 10 th October, 2025, and the then
subsisting auction sale notice of 12th November, 2025.
7. The Section 14 application of the bank was allowed
on  05 th January,  2026  by  the  Additional  District
Magistrate and ultimately on 20 th May 2026, pursuant to
directions in a writ petition by the High Court and
physical possession was also taken by the bank. It is not
disputed that the possession, as on date, is with the
respondent-bank.
8. When matters stood thus, on 19 th June, 2026, the
appellant filed IA No. 2277 of 2026 seeking amendment in
the pending Securitisation Application challenging the
proceedings under Section 14 and the order dated 5 th
January, 2026 of the Additional District Magistrate.  On
11-07-2026, the appellants/borrowers filed IA No. 2575 of
2

--- Page 144 ---
2026 seeking amendment in the pending Securitisation
Application to inter alia place valuation, reserve price,
and certain other incidental matters. On 20th  July, 2026,
the DRT allowed the application seeking amendment, so as
to bring on record the proceedings under Section 14 of
the Act.
9. On 5 th August, 2026, the respondent-bank filed a
Writ Petition, namely, Writ Petition No.9738 of 2026
before  the  High  Court  challenging  the  amendment,  as
ordered on 20th July, 2026.
10. On 5th August, 2026, the first of the two impugned
orders was made, wherein the High Court, on the ground
that the amendment order was without jurisdiction and
moved without condonation of delay application, went on
to stay the proceedings in Securitisation Application
No.578 of 2025.  
11. Further,  on  18th August,  2026,  by  the  second
impugned order, the High Court directed that steps taken
pursuant to the auction sale notice which had since been
issued on 24th June, 2026 would be subject to the outcome
of the Writ Petition.
12. On 20th August, 2026, the bank proceeded with the
auction  and  confirmed  the  sale  in  favour  of  the
successful  bidder,  namely  Bhavik  Choudhary,  who  is
represented before us through learned counsel Shri Naveen
3

--- Page 145 ---
Chomal.
13. On 8 th September, 2026, the respondent-bank has
issued  sale  certificate  in  respect  of  the  mortgaged
property.
14. The  appellants  challenged  the  impugned  orders
before this Court.  When these matters came up before
this Court,  on 10 th September, 2026, we ordered status
quo with regard to nature, title, and possession of the
suit property, while issuing notice.
15. Today, we have heard learned senior counsel for the
parties and learned counsel for the intervenor.
16. The situation, as on today, is that auction is
complete, but the possession is with the respondent-bank.
The securitisation proceedings filed by the appellants,
namely Sarita Shailendra Tiwari and Shailendra Indramani
Tiwari are pending before the DRT. The appellants propose
to  challenge  the  auction  by  impleading  the  auction
purchaser. 
17. We grant the appellants one week's time to do the
needful.
18. Keeping in view the overall facts and circumstances
in mind, we are of the opinion that the DRT should be
directed to dispose of Securitisation Application No. 578
of 2025 pending before it within a period of ten weeks
from today.
4

--- Page 146 ---
19. Pending  the  disposal,  the  respondent-bank  will
continue to retain possession. Considering the nature of
the order made by us, nothing survives for adjudication
in Writ Petition 9738 of 2026 pending before the High
Court. The said Writ Petition will also stand disposed of
in terms of this order.
20. All rights and contentions of parties are left
open. 
21. We also make it clear that the DRT will hear the
Securitisation Application No. 578 of 2025 and all other
pending applications in the amended form, as amended by
the order of 20 th July, 2026. We make it clear that
amendment which was allowed will stand. 
22. The parties to file responses within two weeks from
today.
23. Let the entire matter be disposed of within a
period of 10 weeks from the date of receipt of the order.
24. In view of this, we set aside the impugned orders
of the High Court and treat Writ Petition 9738 of 2026 as
disposed of in terms of this order.
5

--- Page 147 ---
25. The appeals are disposed of in the above terms.
There shall be no order as to costs.

IN THE SUPREME COURT OF INDIA
CIVIL APPELLATE JURISDICTION
CIVIL APPEAL  NO.         OF 2026
(@ SLP(C) No.38532/2025)
  MANGAD NOORUL HIDAYA COMMITTEE                     APPELLANT(S)
                                VERSUS
HAMSA V & ORS.                                     RESPONDENT(S)
O R D E R
1. Leave granted.
2. The present appeal is filed assailing the judgment passed by
the High Court in CRP (Waqf) No.23 of 2025, wherein, the order
of Tribunal was set aside and the original suit was restored.
3. The suit W.O.S. No.65/2023 was instituted by the respondents-
plaintiffs to declare the disputed 88 votes kept with Waqf
Board as invalid, and to direct the Waqf Board to elect the
new Committee based upon remaining 402 votes. A further prayer
was  made  to  remove  122  members  from  general  body  and
restraining  external  members  from  becoming  general  body
members. The Waqf Tribunal, vide order dated 22.04.2025,

--- Page 166 ---
2
returned the plaint on the premise that the Tribunal lacked
jurisdiction to decide the issue relating to the internal
management of the society. The High Court, vide impugned order
dated 06.08.2025, set aside the order of the Tribunal and
restored the suit to its original number and directed the
Tribunal to decide the same, in accordance with law.
4. We have heard the learned Senior counsel appearing for the
appellant  and  the  learned  counsel  appearing  for  the
respondents.
5. The short issue for consideration in this appeal is as to
whether an election dispute would become amenable to be
adjudicated by the Tribunal constituted under the Unified Waqf
Management, Empowerment, Efficiency and Development Act, 1995
(for short, the 1995 Act). 
6. Placing reliance upon Section 6, 7 and 83 of the Act, the
learned Senior counsel appearing for the appellant would
contend that any elections scheduled to be conducted would not
come within the purview of the 1995 Act. 
7. Learned Senior counsel further submits that the issue raised
by the respondents is on the eligibility of the voters,
totalling to 88. Such an issue can only be adjudicated by the
Civil Court having territorial jurisdiction, whose powers are
plenary in nature. 
8. Learned counsel appearing for the respondents placed reliance

--- Page 167 ---
3
on Section 94 read with Section 32(3) of the 1995 Act, in
order to support the impugned judgment passed by the High
Court. 
9. Section 6 of the 1995 Act clearly defines "dispute regarding a
waqf".  Such  a  dispute  is  with  respect  to  the  property
belonging to the waqf or the nature of the waqf, either it is
Shia or Sunni Waqf. Section 7, inter alia deals with the power
of the Tribunal to determine disputes regarding a waqf. Under
Section 83, the State Government shall, by notification,
constitute the Tribunal for deciding any dispute, question or
other matters related to a waqf or waqf property, including
eviction  of  a  tenant  or  determination  of  rights  and
obligations of the lessor and lessee of such property. 
10. Section 32 of the 1995 Act deals with the powers and functions
of the Waqf Board. Such a power has to be exercised in
conjunction with Section 6 and 7 of the 1995 Act. Sub-Section
(3) concerns itself with any scheme of management under Clause
(d), or any direction under clause (e) of Sub-Section (2).
Section 94 navigates a situation where there exists a failure
of mutawalli to discharge his duties.
11. In the case at hand, an interim mutawalli has been appointed
only for the purpose of conducting the election of the
Society. Therefore, neither Section 32 nor Section 94 of the
Act would be applicable, so as to give jurisdiction to the

--- Page 168 ---
4
Tribunal constituted under the Act. 
12. Though the learned counsel appearing for the respondents
submits that such an application has been filed, pursuant to
the direction of the High Court in W.P.(C) No. 15502 of 2023,
inasmuch as there is an inherent lack of jurisdiction, the
said act itself will not facilitate the Waqf Tribunal to
decide the lis. 
13. Furthermore, the High Court in the impugned judgment dated
06.08.2025,  has  not  considered  the  relevant  provisions
governing the matter, and we find that the order is rather
cryptic, without taking note of the issue of jurisdiction
raised. 
14. Taking note of the above, we are inclined to set aside the
impugned judgment only on the ground of lack of jurisdiction.
Consequently, the order of the Waqf Tribunal in W.O.S. No.
65/2023, returning the plaint under Order VII Rule 10 of the
Code of Civil Procedure, 1908, stands confirmed. However, we
make it clear that is well open to the respondents to file a
civil suit in which case they can also press Section 14 of the
Limitation Act, 1963. Such a suit will have to be filed within
a period of one month from the date of receipt of a copy of
this order. We further make it clear that as and when such a
suit is filed as aforestated, we expect the same to be decided
only on merits, and certainly not on the question of delay.

--- Page 169 ---
5
15. The appeal stands allowed, accordingly. 
16. Pending application(s), if any, shall stand disposed of.

  [M.M. SUNDRESH]
       ………………………………………………………………………J.

NEW DELHI;

          UPON hearing the counsel the Court made the following
                             O R D E R
1. On 02.09.2026, following order was passed:
“1. We have heard learned counsel for the
parties  and  perused  the  materials  on
record including the affidavits filed by
the  Secretaries  to  the  Government  of
India,  Ministry  of  Home  Affairs  and
Ministry of Personnel, Public Grievances
and Pensions, Department of Personnel and
Training,  pursuant  to  our  order  dated
28.07.2026, the relevant portion of which
reads as follows:
“2. We direct the Secretaries to the
Government of India, Ministry of Home
Affairs  and  Ministry  of  Personnel,
Public  Grievances  and  Pensions,
Department of Personnel and Training
to  submit  individual  affidavit(s)
detailing the steps taken thus far for
implementation  of  the  directions
issued by this Court vide the judgment
and order dated 23.05.2025 passed in
Civil Appeal No.13104 of 2024 (Sanjay
Prakash & Ors. versus Union of India &
Ors.)  3.  In  the  compliance
affidavit(s),  it  shall  also  be
mentioned as to how many officers have
been  brought  on  deputation  to  the
Central Armed Police Forces (CAPFs),
cadre wise, up to the level of Senior
Administrative  Grade  (SAG),  after
passing  of  the  judgment  and  order
dated 23.05.2025.”
2.  In  the  affidavit  filed  by  the
Secretary to the Government of India,
Ministry of Home Affairs, it is stated
that 46 Indian Police Service (IPS)
officers  have  been  brought  on
deputation to the Central Armed Police
Forces  (CAPFs)  upto  the  level  of
Senior  Administrative  Grade  (SAG)
after  passing  of  the  judgment  on
23.05.2025. The statement furnished by
the  said  respondent  is  extracted
hereunder:
4

--- Page 183 ---
IPS OFFICERS BROUGHT ON DEPUTATION TO
CAPFS UPTO THE LEVEL OF SENIOR
ADMINISTRATIVE GRADE(SAG) AFTER 23.05.2025
Force SP DIG IG TOTAL
BSF - 8 5 13
CISF - 9 2 11
CRPF - 4 5 9
ITBP - 3 3 6
SSB 2 2 3 7
3. Before we pass necessary order(s), we
direct the Secretary to the Government of
India, Ministry of Home Affairs to explain
the above statement, for bringing in IPS
officers on deputation to the five CAPFs;
what  procedure  was  followed  before
bringing the above officers on deputation
i.e., whether any requisition was made by

2. Pursuant to the above order, a compliance affidavit has been
filed.
3. Prior to that, an Affidavit was filed in compliance of the
order dated 28.07.2026 detailing the chronology of events post the
judgment and order of this Court of which violation is alleged.
4. The contempt petitioners have highlighted the infraction of
the directions contained in the subject order, para-wise, in
Appendix-A to the Affidavit filed on 13.10.2026. It is submitted by
5

--- Page 184 ---
them that Act No.9/2026 has no bearing on the direction which
required the contemnor(s)-respondent(s) to carry out the exercise
of cadre review in all CAPFs which was due since 2021 and was
required to be carried out within a period of six months under the
order of which contempt is alleged. Further, our attention has been
invited to the alleged infraction of the direction contained in
paragraph  45(5)  of  the  order  where  under  the  contemnor(s)-
respondent(s) were required to progressively reduce the number of
posts earmarked for deputation in the cadres of CAPFs up to the
level of Senior Administrative Grade (SAG). It is submitted that
though period for such reduction had an outer time limit of two
years, such reduction would have to be in continuum and not by one
stroke on the last date of the time limit set out for such
reduction. It has been urged that there has been a violation of
this direction by fresh inductions through deputation as would be
apparent from the table set out in the order dated 02.09.2026.
5. We notice from the chronology of events set out in the
compliance affidavit that the Home Ministry had issued letters on
26.12.2025  and  03.02.2026  to  all  CAPFs  for  undertaking  a
comprehensive review of their existing Group-A cadres and had
invited proposals in that regard. In this context, it has been
urged on behalf of the petitioners that the outer time limit for
the cadre review was set out as six months whereas here the
proposals were invited after six months which is a flagrant
violation of the directions issued by this Court. Besides, our
attention was also invited to Item No. 10 in the chronology of
events which would indicate that proposals were received in the

IN RE: CONTEMPT AGAINST CHANDAN PRASAD
O R D E R
SPECIAL LEAVE PETITION (CRIMINAL) NO. 6062 OF 2025:
Heard learned counsel for the petitioner and learned
counsel for the respondent no.2.
2. Yesterday, the matter was mentioned by learned counsel
for the petitioner indicating that the order of this Court
dated 29.09.2026 which was passed on a stand of respondent
no.2 that he would take the petitioner with him to Assam
on the very same day, the said commitment was not honoured
1

--- Page 187 ---
SLP (CRL.) NO. 6062/2025
as the petitioner was not taken by the respondent no.2
from the Court and instead copy of the ticket from Delhi
to Assam was forwarded to her by WhatsApp and she was
asked to come directly to the Railway Station, which she
did; but the respondent no.2 never turned up for the
journey. Noting the same, we had directed the matter to be
listed today and also directed for the appearance of the
respondent no.2.
3. Today, learned counsel for the respondent no.2 submits
that he has joined the proceeding virtually as he is in
Assam and could not reach Delhi to be present before
Court, due to there being no means for him to reach Delhi
at such short notice. However, on merits it was submitted
that the respondent no.2 had informed the counsel that he
did not take the petitioner with him because he has given
fresh consideration to the matter and has reached the
conclusion that he cannot live with the petitioner even
for an hour.
4. Be that as it may, we find the Court has been
thoroughly mislead. We are refraining from commenting on
the role of the party concerned, but observe that it is
unfortunate that such type of misrepresentation, not once,
but repeatedly made by the respondent no.2 before the
Trial Court as well as the High Court and even this Court,
with such boldness, has continued.
2

--- Page 188 ---
SLP (CRL.) NO. 6062/2025
5. Coming to the merits of the matter, especially the
fact that there has been total lack of  bonafide on the
part of the respondent no.2, in the opinion of the Court,
a clear cut case of criminal contempt has been made, as it
was on the face of the Court since the undertaking given
repeatedly to this Court, has not been honoured. However,
by way of extraordinary indulgence, we refrain from taking
such extreme step in view of the order which we propose to
pass.
6. Having considered the matter, as the present petition
has been filed seeking cancellation of the anticipatory
bail  granted  to  the  respondent  no.2-husband  of  the
petitioner, we allow the prayer. The Anticipatory Bail
granted to the respondent no.2  vide the impugned order
stands  cancelled.  The  respondent  no.2  shall  surrender
before the Court below positively within one week from
today and shall be taken into judicial custody. The Trial
Court is directed to expedite the trial and take it to its
logical conclusion at the earliest.
7. As the respondent no.2 is also present through virtual
mode, the Court records that he is aware of the order
personally.
3

--- Page 189 ---
SLP (CRL.) NO. 6062/2025
8. Interim order passed by this Court on 29.10.2025
staying all the inter se proceedings pending between the
parties stands vacated.
9. The Special Leave Petition stands disposed of in the
aforementioned terms.
10. Pending  application(s),  if  any,  shall  also  stand
disposed of.
SUO MOTU   CONTEMPT PETITION (CIVIL) NO. 3 OF 2026:  
In view of the order passed above in SLP(Criminal)
No.6062/2025,  the  present  Contempt  Petition  stands
closed.

1

5. The brief facts of the case relevant for the present
issue are that the father of the appellant-Late Ariyappa and

decreed and shares were allotted. After that, the father of
the appellant passed away. In the First Appeal filed by the

the execution case in accordance with law.

Non-Reportable
IN THE SUPREME COURT OF INDIA
CIVIL APPELLATE JURISDICTION
Civil Appeal No.18067 of 2017
Principal Officer LG Electronics
India Pvt. Ltd Thr. Its Authorized
Signatory Mr. Ashish Agrawal
...Appellant
Versus
Assistant Commissioner of
Income Tax, NOIDA and Anr.     
 ...Respondents
W I T H
Civil Appeal No.18068 of 2017
A N D
Civil Appeal No.18281 of 2017
O R D E R
The appellant/assessee under the Income T ax Act, 1961 1 was
concerned with the notice issued under Sections 147/148 of the Act;
which the High Court refused to interfere with and hence the appeal.
2. Essentially the reassessment was proposed for the Assessment
Years 2006-07, 2007-08 and 2008-09 alleging that parent company
of the assessee, M/s L.G. Electronics Korea and other associated
enterprises were running a Permanent Establishment (PE) in India,
thereby obligating the assessee to deduct TDS on the remittances
made to the parent company and the associated enterprises. The
notices  under  Section  148  for  the  relevant  years  are  dated
1 For brevity, “the IT Act”

--- Page 199 ---
28.03.2013, 21.03.2014 and 31.03.2015 produced in the respective
appeals as Annexures P11, P11 and P1.  It was alleged that income
of the assessee had escaped assessment, since the failure to deduct
TDS  brings  in  a  consequence  of  disallowance  of  such  expenses
under Section 40 (a) (i) of the IT Act. 
3. The  assessee  before  the  High  Court  urged  the  ground  of
limitation pointing out that there is nothing to show that income has
escaped assessment due to the failure on the part of the assessee to
disclose complete and full facts or that the assessee was guilty of
concealment of facts. The reassessment thus is reduced to a mere
change of opinion, which cannot be permitted. The Double T axation
Avoidance Agreement (DTAA) between India and Korea was also put
forth along with the other grounds.
4. The Division Bench of the High Court found that proceedings
were taken against the Korean Company and it is related entities to
tax  the  chargeable  income  in  their  hands  and  there  were  also
proceedings initiated against the appellant company under Section
201 of the IT Act for recovery of amount of tax, not deducted at
source.  The  third  consequence,  which  arose  from  the  survey
conducted  under  Section  133A  of  the  IT  Act,  was  the  instant
proceedings to disallow the related expenses under Section 40(a)(i)
for failure to deduct taxes. The Division Bench left the question of
DTAA  to  be  considered  in  the  reassessment  proceedings  and
negatived the contention of limitation; since, there was no disclosure

--- Page 200 ---
with  respect  to  the  Permanent  Establishment  of  the  Korean
Company  operating  in  India.  The  notice  under  Section  148  for
initiating reassessment proceedings under Section 147 does not call
for any interference, held the impugned order.
5. Sri Deepak Chopra, Learned Senior Counsel for the assessee,
pointed  out that the reassessment  proceedings were carried  out
and, in an appeal, there was an order under Section 250 of IT Act
communicated, without anything written on the same and enclosing
two blank papers. The assessee’s further appeal was frustrated, and
it is informed that the incumbent CIT (Appeals) NOIDA, who issued
the blank order, was later suspended. As of now, unless the notice
issued under Section 148 is interfered with, the assessee would be
left remediless.
6. Sri  Raghavendra  P .  Shankar,  learned  Additional  Solicitor
General,  on  the  other  hand,  pointed  out  that  the  parallel
proceedings initiated under Section 201 stand allowed in favour of
the  assessee  by  the  Income  T ax  Appellate  T ribunal  (ITAT).  What
remains is for the appellant to produce the said order either before
the  officer  who  conducted  the  reassessment  or  in  an  appeal
instituted,  which  could  be  reckoned  to  delete  the  disallowance
carried out on this ground. The learned ASG would contend that
since reassessment order is not produced, he is unable to assist as
to whether there were other grounds on which reassessment was
carried out.

--- Page 201 ---
7. The order of the ITAT from the proceedings under Section 201 is
produced as Annexure A1 in I.A. No.118536 of 2025 in C.A. No.18067
of 2017. From a reading of the order, we find that the proceedings
initiated  under  Section  201  were  taken  in  appeal  and  on  the
directions of the Dispute Resolution Panel (DRP), the First Appellate
Authority modified the order, determining profits at 20% markup on
50%  salary  cost  of  the  expatriate  employees,  attributed  to  the
Permanent Establishment of L.G. Korea, in India. It was also noticed
that the assessment proceedings initiated against L.G. Korea was
quashed by the ITAT for non-implementation of the directions of the
DRP . The said appellate orders for the assessment years 2005-06 to
2010-11 were not challenged, since it had low tax effect. The ITAT, in
the proceedings under Section 201, held that there is no tax liability
on the payee i.e. L.G. Korea and hence there is no obligation on the
assessee  to  withhold  tax  under  Section  195  of  the  Act.  The
appellant/assessee  was  found  not  liable  to  be  treated  as  an
‘assessee-in-default’ under Section 201 of the Act. If the assessee
cannot be treated as an ‘assessee-in-default’ under Section 201,
necessarily there cannot be any disallowance made under Section
40(a)(i)  of  the  IT  Act  and  hence  even  if  the  reassessment
proceedings have been carried out, we are of the opinion that it
requires no remand to the Assessing Officer.
8. We also take note of the submission of ASG that there could be

--- Page 202 ---
other  grounds  on  which  reassessment  was  actually  carried  out,
which we cannot subscribe to. The notice under Section 147 was
only  with  respect  to  the  default  under  Section  201  and  the
disallowance of the expenses claimed under Section 40(a)(i) of the
Act. If the ground on which reassessment is found to be initiated is
untenable, then there is no question of any other ground coming
forth in the reassessment proceedings being utilized for the purpose
of determining  escapement of income.  We,  hence, hold  that the
reassessment  proceedings  initiated  are  unenforceable  for  the
assessment years 2006-07 to 2008-09.  The appellant shall produce
our decision and the decision of the ITAT produced as Annexure A1
under Section 201 proceedings before the Assessing Officer who
shall close the reassessment proceedings as unenforceable.
9. The appeals are allowed.
10. Pending application(s), if any, shall stand rejected.
.......…….……………………. J.
              (J. B. PARDIWALA)
....……….……………………. J.

IN THE SUPREME COURT OF INDIA
CIVIL APPELLATE JURISDICTION 
CIVIL APPEAL NOS. 13388-13389  OF 2026
(@ SPECIAL LEAVE PETITION (CIVIL) NOS.21392-21393 OF 2026)
VIJAY GANAPATI                                     APPELLANT(S)
                                VERSUS
CHITRA GANAPATI                                    RESPONDENT(S)
O R D E R
Heard the petitioner in-person.
2. From  the  records  it  transpires  that  the  sole
respondent had refused to accept the notice sent by this
Court and thus, notice on her stood deemed to have been
served.
3. Leave granted.
4. The appellant is aggrieved by the order impugned dated
23.01.2026 passed in Civil Revision No.691/2026 by which
permission to amend his pleadings with regard to bringing
on record the details of the immovable property held by
his late father and for incorporation of a relief based on
the judgment in the probate case dated 24.02.2021, has
been partly allowed, inasmuch as, the amendment has been
allowed only with regard to his pleadings relating to
immovable  property,  but  not  for  incorporation  of  the
1

--- Page 211 ---
probate judgment. Review application filed against the
said order was also dismissed vide order dated 19.03.2026
in Review Application No. RA-CR-15/2026, which is also
impugned herein. 
5. It was submitted that the parties are the adopted
children of Late Shri. R. Ganpati and upon his death, the
appellant had filed a Suit for injunction and declaration
against the respondent with regard to a property, which
according to him, was required to be divided equally among
both the parties. In the said Civil Suit the respondent
had  filed  a  Will  dated  20.12.2000  bequeathing  the
appellant’s share in the suit property in favour of the
respondent. This prompted the appellant to seek amendment
in  his  plaint  disputing  the  Will  which  was  allowed.
However, in the meantime, the respondent-defendant sought
probate of the Will which was executed according to her by
her late father on 20.12.2000. The same upon trial was
dismissed by judgment dated 24.02.2021 and according to
the  appellant,  the  same  had  attained  finality.  The
appellant then moved the Trial Court under Order VI Rule
17 of the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908 seeking amendment
of the plaint by seeking to incorporate a relief based on
the  judgment  dated  24.02.2021  passed  in  the  probate
proceedings.
6. The Trial Court dismissed the said application and the
High Court in CR No. 1335/2025 directed the Trial Court to
2

--- Page 212 ---
pass fresh order after considering all the pleas raised by
the appellant.
7. The Trial Court by order dated 01.10.2025 partly
allowed the prayer of the appellant to amend his pleadings
with  regard  to  the  movable  properties  and  the  share
claimed  therein  but  disallowed  the  amendment  sought
pertaining to incorporation of the probate judgment. The
review petition filed by the appellant was also dismissed
on 18.10.2025.
8. Thereafter, the appellant moved before the High Court
by filing Civil Revision No.691/2026 in which the impugned
order has been passed.
9. Learned counsel for the appellant submitted that once
the probate sought by the respondent had been dismissed,
such fact is a necessary issue for consideration in the
Suit filed by the appellant and not allowing incorporation
of such plea in the plaint, will cause damage to the
appellant’s case, that too, when clearly the law is in his
favour.
10. We have considered the matter and gone through the
material on record. In view of the dismissal of the Suit
seeking probate of the Will in favour of the respondent
having  attained  finality,  and  also  in  the  written
statement  in  the  suit  filed  by  the  appellant,  the
respondent has placed reliance on the said Will, we find
that the judgment of the Court dated 24.02.2021 dismissing
3

--- Page 213 ---
the Suit for probate of the Will was required to be
brought on record and rightly by way of an amendment as
sought by the appellant.
11. For the reasons aforesaid, the appeals are allowed.
The amendment as sought by the appellant stands allowed.
Consequences to follow.
12. Pending application(s), if any, shall stand disposed
of.

Heard learned counsel for the parties.
2. Leave granted.
3. The present appeal arises out of an order dated
19.07.2024 passed by the High Court of Kerala at
Ernakulam in MACA No.3050 of 2015, assailing the order
dated 23.05.2015 passed by the Additional District and
Additional MACT Judge IV, Pathanamthitta (MACT), by
which a compensation of Rs.39,91,356/- (Rupees Thirty
Nine Lakhs Ninety One Thousand Three Hundred and Fifty
Six) with 9% interest per annum awarded by the MACT,
has been reduced to Rs.31,99,436/- (Rupees Thirty One
1

--- Page 221 ---
Civil Appeal No. 13583/2026
Lakhs Ninety Nine Thousand Four Hundred and Thirty Six)
while maintaining the rate of interest.
4. Learned counsel for the appellant submits that the
appellant at the time of the accident was aged 21 years
and was a vegetable vendor. It was submitted that the
admitted position is that he is half paralyzed and the
entire right side including the hand and he is blind in
the right eye. It was contended that the same has also
resulted in loss of marriage prospects, which for all
practical purposes seems to have been foreclosed and
the amount awarded is only Rs.1,00,000/- (Rupees One
Lakh) under that head. Learned counsel contended that
the functional disability taken by the MACT as 95% has
been reduced to 80%, whereas it should have been 100%,
as the entire right side is paralyzed. It was further
contented that the amount of loss of income as computed
by the MACT was just and proper and ought not to have
been reduced in the manner it has been done by the High
Court and future prospects being reduced from 50% to
40% also needs interference. It was his contention that
for future treatment when clearly the appellant has
many years left of his life, an amount of Rs.1,50,000/-
(Rupees  One  Lakh  and  Fifty  Thousand)  is  totally
2

--- Page 222 ---
Civil Appeal No. 13583/2026
inadequate.

relevant  aspects  while  passing  the  order.  It  was

taking a multiplier of 18, which is just and proper, an
additional amount of loss of wages for 48 months has
also been computed by the MACT, which the High Court
has rightly held to be double load on the Insurance
Company  and  thus,  the  same  may  not  require
interference.  
6. Having considered the matter, we find that many
heads require enhancement, and may be on some heads the
order of the High Court reducing the amount as has been
granted by the MACT, may have some justification.
However, on an overall analysis, we find that the ends
of justice would be served by not getting into the
details of the computation restoring the amount awarded
by the MACT would be fair and just in the facts and
circumstances of the present case.
7. Accordingly, for the reasons aforesaid, the appeal
is allowed. The order impugned passed by the High Court
is set aside and the order dated 23.05.2015 passed by
3

O R D E R
1. Leave granted.
2. This  appeal  takes  exception  to  the  order  dated
21.08.2026 passed by the learned Single Judge, High Court
of  Madhya  Pradesh,  Bench  at  Gwalior  in  Miscellaneous
Criminal Case No.32428/2026 whereby the petition preferred
by the appellant and the proforma respondent no.3 seeking
quashing of the FIR bearing Crime No.73/2022 at P.S. Padav,
District Gwalior for the offences punishable under Sections
420 and 34 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 ('IPC' for short)
has been dismissed.
3. The FIR aforestated came to be lodged at the instance
of respondent no.2, Dr. Amarjit Singh Bhalla.
4. Before  the  High  Court,  the  appellant  and  the
respondent no.3-complainant had prayed for quashing of the
aforesaid FIR based on a compromise. During the pendency of
the  petition,  IA  Nos.13532/2026  and  13534/2026  were
preferred by the parties duly supported by their affidavits
1

--- Page 236 ---
praying that the matter should be disposed of in terms of
the compromise. The factum of compromise was duly verified
by the Registrar of the High Court.
5. The High Court recorded in the impugned order that
the parties had voluntarily, without any threat, inducement
and coercion, arrived at a compromise.
6. In  spite  thereof,  the  quashing  petition  stands
rejected by the High Court on the premise that the offences
alleged were compoundable and hence, the parties would be
better advised to approach the trial Court by way of a
compounding application.
7. Being aggrieved, the appellant is before us by way of
the instant appeal. The respondent no.2-complainant is duly
represented before this Court by Mr. Yashraj Singh Bundela,
learned counsel.
8. Before the High Court and in this Court as well, the
complainant has made a categorical statement that the
disputes have been settled between the parties and the FIR
should be quashed. The dispute between the parties is a
purely private one arising from monetary transactions. 
9. In this background, we are of the view that there was
no reason whatsoever for the High Court to have relegated
the parties to the trial Court for moving an application
for compounding of the offences. Rejection of the quashing
petition under Section 528 of the BNSS and directing the
parties to move the trial Court in spite of the settlement
duly verified by the Registrar of High Court was not
2

--- Page 237 ---
justified in view of the judgment of this Court in case of

to quash the proceedings.

IN THE SUPREME COURT OF INDIA
CIVIL APPELLATE JURISDICTION
CIVIL APPEAL NO.13234/2026
[ARISING OUT OF SLP (C) NO.29614/2025]
SHANKAR NAYAK                                 Appellant(s)
VERSUS
RIYAZ MANSOORI AND ANR. Respondent(s)
1. RIYAZ MANSOORI; AND
2. THE NEW INDIA INSURANCE COMPANY LTD.      
O R D E R
Heard learned counsel for the parties.
2. Leave granted.
3. The present appeal arises out of an order dated
15.04.2024 passed by the High Court of Madhya Pradesh,
Bench at Indore in Misc. Appeal No.3421/2022 by which the
challenge made by the appellant­victim to the compensation
awarded by the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Indore
(hereinafter referred to as the "MACT") resulted in an
increase, but the same not being to the satisfaction of
the appellant, the present appeal has been preferred.
4. Learned counsel for the appellant submits that the
accident has left him in a position where his both hands
and feet practically cannot be used for any purposes much
less for earning of employment. 
1

--- Page 273 ---
5. It was submitted that at the time of accident, the
appellant was a manual labourer and was somehow managing
to earn a living for his family but for the last 10 years
he has been totally dependent on others.
6. Learned counsel for the appellant contended that the
Court may take into consideration the fact that now the
appellant being 60 years has still quite a few years left
of his life and the entire sustenance for that period
would be the money he would get as compensation as there
is no other source of livelihood/income for the family.
7. Learned counsel for the Insurance Company submitted
that the High Court has taken care of the condition of the
appellant   and   thus,   enhanced   the   compensation   from
Rs.2,89,600/­ (Rupees Two Lakh Eighty Nine Thousand and
Six Hundred) to Rs.10,54,880/­ (Rupees Ten Lakh Fifty Four
Thousand Eight Hundred and Eighty) which is sufficient in
the facts and circumstances of the present case.
8. Learned counsel further submitted that the condition
in   which   the   appellant   is   would   not   require   more
compensation to be awarded in the facts and circumstances
of the present case.
9. Though, under the various heads, we find that the
High   Court   ought   to   have   been   more   reasonable   and
practical while awarding the compensation, but for the
purposes of convenience, we round off the figure without
2

--- Page 274 ---
going   into   the   exact   details   of   the   computation   of
compensation under various heads. Accordingly, we find
that the interest of justice would be served by awarding
an amount of Rs.15,00,000/­ (Rupees Fifteen Lakh) while
maintaining the rate of interest at 7% per annum to be
taken from the date of filing of the present appeal.
10. Ordered   accordingly.   The   appellant   be   paid   the
amount as directed above, after adjusting whatever which
may have been paid during the interregnum, within six
weeks from today.
11. The   appeal   stands   disposed   of   in   the   aforesaid
terms.
. . . . . . . . . . . .,J
[AHSANUDDIN AMANULLAH]

1. This appeal is against the judgment of the High Court of
Andhra Pradesh in Second Appeal No. 939 of 2002 dated 18.08.2011.
The appellant filed a suit for perpetual injunction to restrain the
defendant from interfering with his property. The Trial Court by
its judgment dated 21.12.2000 dismissed the suit. The appellant
filed  an  appeal  which  came  to  be  dismissed  by  order  dated
30.09.2002. The appellant filed a Second Appeal which also came to
be dismissed by the order impugned before us.
2. Heard  Mr.  A.D.N.  Rao,  learned  senior  counsel  for  the
appellant(s). Having considered the matter in detail, we are of the
opinion that the concurrent findings of fact by the Trial and
Appellate Court have not given rise to any substantial question of
law for the High Court to exercise its jurisdiction under Section
100 of the Civil Procedure Code, 1908. We are of the opinion that
the High Court was justified in dismissing the Second Appeal. Civil
Appeal is dismissed. 
3. As  the  present  appeal  arises  out  of  a  suit  for  bare
injunction, the appellant(s) are at liberty to adopt such remedies

and disposed of on their own merits.

7. The issue before us pertains to the non-inclusion of third
gender in the notifications for vacancies issued by the respondent
State. In order to address the issue at hand, it is necessary to
make the following inquires:-
QUESTIONS TO BE ADDRESSED:-
I. Which Recruitment Rules govern the vacancy notifications,
such as the one annexed as Annexure P-7 in the petition by
Jane Kaushik , issued by the Delhi Subordinate Services
Selection Board, Government of NCT of Delhi (for short,
“DSSSB”)? 
a. Whether the said Recruitment Rules are traceable to
any  constitutional  provision,  or  statutory
enactment, or State Service Rules. In other words,
where does the DSSSB derive powers to issue the
notifications of vacancies in respect of teaching
roles for specific subjects?

--- Page 302 ---
3
II. Whether  the  aforesaid  Recruitment  rules,  or  statutory
enactment, or State Service Rules require that vacancies in
respect of teaching roles be notified on the basis of
gender? 
III. If the answer to the above question is in negative, then,
what forms the basis for bifurcation of vacancies between
male and female candidates in a vacancy notification issued
by the DSSSB? In other words, what is the objective behind
notifying vacancies separately for males and females? 
IV. If the answer to Q.2 is in affirmative, then, what forms
the basis for using gender as a basis for notifying
vacancies in public recruitment? 
V. In both the petitions, do the respondents propose to
include third gender in vacancy notifications issued by
them  through  DSSSB?  In  other  words,  in  what  manner
transgender  persons  would  be  accommodated  in  public
employment?
VI. In the petition by Praveen Singh, insofar as the question
of age relaxation is concerned, why the High Court did not
deem it fit to exercise its power under Rule 12 of the
Delhi High Court Establishment (Appointment and Conditions
of Service) Rules, 1972, to provide age relaxation to
transgender  persons  considering  the  socio-economic
discrimination that they face?

are part of the same biker gang.  
3. It is contended that the petitioners were not

primarily arise out of confession of co-accused
given to the police which is inadmissible in
nature. It is also pertinent that the FIR is of

2023, the proclamation under Section 82 of The

substantial to rope in the petitioners.

petitioners can be released on anticipatory bail.

O R D E R
Heard learned counsel for the petitioner/applicant in IA No.
70727/2026.
2. The said application has been filed seeking modification of
the order dated 10.02.2026 passed in SLP (C) No. 14600 of 2025.
3. We note that basically the grievance of the petitioner is
reflected from paragraph No. 12 of the application, which reads as
under:
“That it is therefore just, necessary and in the
interest of justice that this Hon'ble Court be pleased
to clarify that the proceedings before it pertained to
the  reasonableness  of  the  quantum  of  maintenance,
especially the fixation of Rs. 3,000/- per month for the
Petitioner-Wife, and not to the reasonableness of the
quantum of arrears or the instalment schedule as an
issue,  and  further  clarify  that  the  maintenance
liability  of  the  Respondent-Husband  stands  at  Rs.
7,000/- per month in terms of the order dated 17.09.2024
passed under Section 127 CrPC, as specifically pleaded
in the Additional Affidavit dated 01.12.2025.”
4. Learned counsel for the applicant/petitioner submits that in
the order of this Court dated 10.02.2026 the amount of interim
maintenance to be paid by the respondent-husband to the applicant-
petitioner wife is typed as Rs. 5,500/- (Rupees Five Thousand Five
Hundred) per month, which is an inadvertent typographical error, as
the said amount is Rs. 7,000/- (Rupees Seven Thousand) per month.
5. We have perused the record and find the contention to be

--- Page 325 ---
3
M.A. (C) No. 3048/2026
correct, especially in view of the order passed by the  Principal
Judge, Family Court, Patiala in the underlying case bearing CRM
No.861/2019 wherein vide order dated 17.09.2024 maintenance of
Rs. 7,000/- (Rupees Seven Thousand) was filed under Section 127 of
Cr.P.C.
6. We note that a copy of the application has been duly served on
the learned counsel for the respondent.
7. Having considered the matter, the prayer is allowed. The
amount of Rs. 5,500/- (Rupees Five Thousand Five Hundred) indicated
in the order dated 10.02.2026 passed in SLP (C) No. 14600 of 2025,
stands substituted by Rs. 7,000/- (Rupees Seven Thousand).
8. In the facts and circumstances of the case and what has been
stated at paragraph No. 12 of the present application, we clarify
that as the present matter relates to the fixing of interim
maintenance, the Court, while deciding the final maintenance, shall
not be prejudiced by these proceedings and shall independently
apply its mind while fixing the quantum of maintenance.  IA No.
70727/2026 stands disposed of.
9. As  a  consequence,  Miscellaneous  application  also  stands
disposed of.
10. Pending applications, if any, also stand disposed of.

SUSHILA                                            Petitioner(s)
                                VERSUS
STATE OF RAJASTHAN                                 Respondent(s)
office report for direction is to be listed. 
 
Date : 16-10-2026 This petition was called on for hearing today.
CORAM : 
         HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE MANMOHAN 
                       [IN CHAMBER]
For Petitioner(s) : Mr. P. K. Jain- 505, AOR
                   
                   Mr. Sachin Sharma- 2538, AOR
                   Mr. Anil Kumar Gulati, Adv.                   
                   
For Respondent(s) : 
          UPON hearing the counsel the Court made the following
                             O R D E R
1. The present SLP (Crl.) No.7592 of 2013 was dismissed on 23 rd
August 2013 on account of petitioner’s failure to file surrender
certificate within two weeks as directed by this Court vide order
dated 08th August 2013.
2. Subsequently, the petitioner was arrested on 18 th February
2026. Thereafter, the petitioner filed applications for restoration
being I.A. No.187034 of 2026, application for condonation of delay
in filing the application for restoration being I.A. No.187037 of
  Page 1 of 3

--- Page 360 ---
2026, Bail application being I.A. No.187041 of 2026 as well as
application for exemption from filing official English translation
being I.A. No. 187043 of 2026 and application for exemption from
filing SLP paper books being I.A. No. 200497 of 2026 in M.A.
No.2651 of 2026.
3. A Coordinate Bench of this Court vide order dated 25 th August
2026  condoned  the  delay  and  allowed  the  application  for
restoration. The SLP was directed to be listed during the next
week. However, no order was passed on the application for exemption
from filing SLP paper book.
4. As the original paper book and the original file record had
been weeded out, the complete SLP paper book was not available with
the Registry. However, as the counsel for the petitioner did not
have in his possession a copy of the initial SLP filed by the
petitioner, the matter was again listed before this Court.
5. On 16th September 2026, the Registry of this Court was directed
to file a detailed report as to why even a scanned copy of Special
Leave Petition (Crl.) No.7592 of 2013 was not available.  
6. In pursuance to the order dated 16 th September 2026, Scanning
Cell has furnished a report dated 26 th September 2026 stating
therein that weeded out file was scanned as per the prevailing
practice and in accordance with Order LVI, Part VII, Rule 5 of the
Supreme Court Rules, 2013 which is reproduced hereinudner -
“5. All papers forming the record relating to
admission  matters  including  petitions  for
  Page 2 of 3

--- Page 361 ---
preliminary  hearing,  objections,  rejoinder  and
documents (except original documents), if any, and
such like matters may not be retained in the
Registry beyond one year of their disposal. Only
the index of documents filed, original documents
and the order disposing of the petitions may be
preserved permanently and the rest of the papers
discarded and destroyed in the manner indicated in
Rule 8.”
7. Further, the report states that a weeded scanned copy of the
instant matter is available in the Scanning Cell repository of
disposed matters.  
8. However, a perusal of the scanned copy reveals that only the
first four pages and the Orders passed by this Court have been
preserved and not the entire paper book in particular the SLP as
well as its annexures.  
9. Prima facie,  it appears that the prevailing practice of
partially preserving the record as well as the above stated Rule
are violative of the Article 129 of the Constitution of India which
mandates that the Supreme Court shall be a Court of Record.
10. In view of the above, Registry is directed to list the matter
before the Regular Bench after two weeks. 
(NEETU SACHDEVA)                                (ANJALI PANWAR)
DEPUTY REGISTRAR                              ASSISTANT  REGISTRAR

          UPON hearing the counsel the Court made the following
                             O R D E R
1. The petitioner seeks cancellation of bail granted to Aditya
Dev Pathak (respondent No.2) by the High Court in connection
with FIR 412 of 2023 at Chinhat PS, Lucknow East for offence
punishable under Sections 302 & 201 of the Indian Penal Code,
1860 and Sections 3 & 25 of the Arms Act, 1959.
2. Respondent  No.2  is  accused  of  committing  the  murder  of
petitioner’s daughter with an illegal pistol resulting in her
death. A charge sheet is filed and a trial is underway.
3. The High Court granted bail to the accused on the ground that
five eyewitnesses had turned hostile in trial. 
4. In X v. State of Rajasthan, 2024 SCC OnLine SC 3539 , it was
observed  that  when  the  trial  is  underway  courts  should
ordinarily be loath to grant bail in case of serious offences.
5. Considering that a material witness remains to be examined in
the trial, and the serious allegations against respondent
No.2,  we  are  of  the  opinion  that  the  bail  granted  to
2

--- Page 400 ---
SLP(Crl.) No.18193/2026
respondent No.2 ought to be cancelled. The Respondent No. 2 is
directed to surrender before the jurisdictional Court within a
period of two weeks from today. In the event of failure to do
so, the trial Court shall take appropriate steps in accordance
with law to secure his custody. Ordered accordingly.
6. In the aforesaid, the impugned order is herereby set aside. 
7. The Special Leave Petition stands disposed of accordingly.
8. Pending application(s), if any, shall stand disposed of.

          UPON hearing the counsel the Court made the following
                             O R D E R
1. The petitioner seeks cancellation of bail granted to Pawan
Kumar  Yadav  (respondent  No.1)  by  the  High  Court  in
connection with FIR 619 0f 2025 under offence punishable
under Sections 61(2)(a), 109(1), 190, 191(2), 191(3) of the
Bhartiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 registered at Kotwali Ayodhya
PS, District Ayodhya (Faizabad).
2. The respondent no.1 is accused of conspiring with other co-
accused persons in an attempt to murder the petitioner by
shooting him with a pistol. Specifically, the respondent
no.1 is alleged to have provided the pistol and cartridges
used in the attack. A charge sheet has been filed and the
trial is underway. 
3. Respondent No.1 was enlarged on bail on the ground that
there are no allegations that he fired shots upon the
petitioner  and  the  only  material  against  him  is  the
inadmissible confessional statement of a co-accused. 
4. However, a perusal of the Counter-affidavit filed by the
State of Uttar Pradesh reveals that during investigation,
the Petitioner who was conscious throughout the firing
2

--- Page 406 ---
SLP(Crl.) No.17774/2026
specifically stated that he saw respondent no.1 before the
incident occurred. Furthermore, respondent No.1 has twenty-
six criminal antecedents.
5. Hence, we are of the opinion that the bail granted to
respondent No.1 ought to be cancelled. The Respondent No. 1
is directed to surrender before the jurisdictional Court
within a period of two weeks from today. In the event of
failure to do so, the trial Court shall take appropriate
steps in accordance with law to secure his custody. Ordered
accordingly.
6. In the aforesaid, the impugned order is herereby set aside.
7. The Special Leave Petition stands disposed of accordingly.
8. Pending application(s), if any, shall stand disposed of.

been taken back into service and has now served for more
than 13 years after the passing of the impugned order.

Ld. Principal Judge, Family Court, Hyderabad, Telangana; and/or

the respondent(s), who has no objection to the transfer of the case, this Court is
inclined to allow the transfer petition as prayed for by the petitioner.

bearing HMA No.555 of 2026 titled as “ Gautam Mohan Swaroop vs. Meenakshi
Sareen”,  pending  before  the  Principal  Judge,  Family  Court-02,  Central,  Tis
Hazari Courts, Delhi is ordered to be transferred to the Principal Judge, Family
Court, Hyderabad, Telangana.

         UPON hearing the counsel, the Court made the following
                             O R D E R
The matter requires to be heard insofar as the High Court’s
direction to initiate criminal prosecution against the petitioner
in 17 cases is concerned. However, we find from the observations
made by the Division Bench that the West Bengal State Electricity
Distribution Company Limited itself wanted to initiate disciplinary
proceedings against the petitioner, independent of the direction of
the learned Judge in that regard. 
That being so, the employer cannot be interdicted from taking
steps to initiate disciplinary proceeding against the petitioner in
accordance with the relevant regulations. 
To that extent, the stay order dated 14.10.2025 granted by
this Court shall stand vacated and shall continue to operate only
in the context of initiation of criminal proceedings. 
Needless to state, the disciplinary authorities shall not be
influenced by any observations made either by the learned Judge or
by the Division Bench but would be at liberty to place reliance on
the material collected and collated pursuant to the said orders. 
Re-list on 26.02.2027 with the understanding that the matter
will be taken up after completion of the hearing in all the other
matters.

Heard learned counsel for the parties.
2. After some arguments, in view of the admitted position
that the respondent is earning at least Rs.1,75,000/-
1

--- Page 542 ---
SLP (CRL.) NO. 15061/2025
(Rupees One Lakh Seventy Five Thousand) per month and the
petitioner is his autistic minor daughter, coupled with
the fact that as of now she is getting only Rs.5,000/-
(Rupees Five Thousand) per month for her maintenance from
the respondent-father, we direct that w.e.f. November,
2026, by way of an interim arrangement, an amount of
Rs.25,000/- (Rupees Twenty Five Thousand) per month shall
be paid by the respondent to the petitioner. The payment

--- Page 694 ---
2. The loan accounts were taken in the name of one C. Shanthammal
and D. Raju. Though, it is stated that the proceeds of the sale
were adjusted to the loan accounts and there is still outstanding
in the loan accounts, no figures are specifically furnished of the
outstanding. It is also seen that the proceeds of the sale of
property mortgaged in one loan account had been adjusted in another
loan account. There is also a statement that insofar as D. Raju’s
loan account is concerned, the property belonging to D. Ratchaka
was sold.
3. In the above circumstance, we direct the Branch Manager to
file an affidavit clearly indicating the loans availed by the two
persons namely C. Shanthammal and D. Raju, subject matter of the
CBI investigation and trial along with the orders in the DRT and
the details of the properties mortgaged with the name of the title
holder and the guarantors in the two loan accounts. A statement of
account showing the amounts due as on the date of sale of the
respective properties, with reference to both the accounts, shall
also be placed on record along with the outstanding dues in the
said accounts, if at all there is any, as of now. It shall also be
specified as to what was the outstanding dues after adjustment of
the proceeds from the auction sale of the properties. An affidavit
shall be placed on record within four weeks from today.

--- Page 728 ---
2
3. It is the case of the prosecution that the petitioner obtained

4. We are informed that on similar applications filed with
respect to identical allegations by certain others, this Court
has  granted  anticipatory  bail.  Hence  on  a  prima  facie
consideration of the material on record, we are of the opinion
that the petitioner can be released on anticipatory bail.

the Investigating Officer (for short “I.O.”) may deem fit
impose, on condition also of continued cooperation in the
investigation.

directions issued by the I.O. or summons issued by the
Additional Sessions Judge, Gaya (the jurisdictional court),
the petitioner shall appear before the jurisdictional court
and furnish bail bonds and ensure due appearance in the trial.
